profile.campus: Austin, Travis County, Texas (CyrusOne AUS3 building)
profile.reading:
CyrusOne Austin III sits at 7100 Metropolis Drive in the Met Center business park in southeast Austin, Travis County, Texas, a short drive from Austin Bergstrom International Airport and immediately adjacent to CyrusOne's earlier Austin II building at 7301 Metropolis Drive on the same site. CyrusOne announced the project on April 3, 2015, described in trade press coverage from Data Center Dynamics as up to 172,000 square feet of shell space, including up to 120,000 square feet of colocation space and up to 25,000 square feet of office space, with up to 12 megawatts of power capacity, and called at the time the company's largest facility in the Austin market. CyrusOne commissioned the completed building in mid 2016, and trade coverage from the real estate publication Commercial Property Executive describing that commissioning quotes then CyrusOne chief marketing officer Scott Brueggeman and states the finished facility offers up to 18 megawatts of power capacity, a different figure from the 12 megawatts reported at the 2015 announcement. Both figures come from named trade publications rather than from a data center aggregator, and this registry has not attempted to reconcile the difference, which may reflect a revised design between announcement and completion or simply differing reporting practices. The building was designed with 2N electrical redundancy and marketed alongside CyrusOne's National Internet Exchange interconnection platform, giving tenants access to the company's other Texas and national facilities.

CyrusOne's own current marketing page groups this building with Austin II as a single Austin, Texas campus, stating 242,000 square feet of combined technical IT space and 19 megawatts of combined total IT capacity across both buildings together, a two building campus total that CyrusOne does not break down by building. That combined figure is recorded here as campus context rather than assigned to Austin III individually, consistent with how this registry treats every other CyrusOne multi building campus. No operator disclosure more recent than the 2015 and 2016 figures above addresses this specific building's current square footage or power capacity, and no utility feed size, standby generation, or onsite generation figure specific to Austin III was found in any source reviewed.

CyrusOne, the operator, was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, was bought by private equity firm ABRY Partners in 2007, was purchased by Cincinnati Bell for 525 million dollars in 2010, completed an initial public offering as a real estate investment trust in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired the company for approximately 15 billion dollars. Texas's lack of a state corporate income tax and its position at a major interstate fiber crossroads have helped make it, alongside Northern Virginia, one of CyrusOne's largest US concentrations of facilities, spanning campuses in Austin, the Dallas Fort Worth area, Houston, and a fast growing cluster of buildings in San Antonio. No zoning case, tax abatement filing, or contested public hearing specific to the Austin III address was found in Austin or Travis County public records, consistent with Met Center's status as an already zoned, established business and industrial park. The building sits inside a city now actively writing new rules for the data center industry as a category, with Austin City Council opening work in August 2026, according to Texas Tribune reporting, on a dedicated data center zoning classification, water and noise standards, and a stated council position against incentivizing new data center construction, a debate driven chiefly by concern over prospective large hyperscale campuses elsewhere in the region rather than by this established, already built facility, which was not named in any account of that debate found.

reading.body:
The CyrusOne Austin Data Center III has no confirmed individual power capacity recorded, only a note that the Austin campus as a whole publishes 19 MW of IT capacity.

CyrusOne operates this facility as a privately held company following its 2022 acquisition by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners for approximately 15 billion dollars. The facility sits on Metropolis Drive in Travis County alongside a neighboring data center, both part of a multi-building campus. The company holds relevant security certifications including SSAE 16, HIPAA, and FISMA, indicating the facility serves regulated workloads.

The absence of a facility-specific power figure limits visibility into how much compute this building actually supports. The published 19 MW for the entire Austin campus does not tell whether this third building carries most of that load or a small fraction. For tracking the binding constraint of power on AI scaling, individual facility capacity matters more than campus totals.

The ownership shift to private equity in 2022 means this facility no longer reports performance data to public markets. The CME Group transaction history shows how critical individual data center locations can be for financial infrastructure, but provides no current detail on whether this Austin building serves similar mission-critical tenants or the types of workloads it now hosts.
